title: Blood clotting test
what: A blood test that shows how fast your blood clots. Blood is taken from a vein.
why: Before surgery and childbirth, for bruising or bleeding with no clear cause, to check blood thinner medicines, and during pregnancy.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: Blood thinners and aspirin. They affect the result
If you ever had blood clots or heavy bleeding
If blood draws make you feel unwell, or you have fainted before

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually the test is done on an empty stomach, 8 to 12 hours after eating. You can drink plain water. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Do not eat fatty food or drink alcohol. Do not smoke for at least 1 hour before the test.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your medicines. If you take medicines for your blood, tell your doctor. The doctor decides what to do.

prepare.title: Before the draw
prepare.text: Sit quietly for 10 to 15 minutes. Do not rush.

bring: A list of the medicines you take
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on a support
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped, and a needle goes into a vein
Blood is collected into one or more tubes
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a mosquito bite
Sometimes you feel a bit dizzy. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes. Do not bend your arm
A bruise can appear. It goes away on its own
You can eat and go back to your day right away
Your doctor will explain the results

faq.q: Do I need an empty stomach for a clotting test?
faq.a: Usually yes, 8 to 12 hours after eating. You can drink water. Your clinic will tell you the exact rules.
It is a measure of blood clotting. It is often checked in people who take blood thinners, to find the right dose.

reminders.text: Blood clotting test tomorrow. It is usually done on an empty stomach: no food after dinner, only water. No alcohol or fatty food.
